why: Odd-power-of-y terms cancel, leaving k = 0, 2, ..., 100, i.e. 51 terms; sympy expansion of (x+y)^100 + (x-y)^100 returns exactly 51 monomials.
(1+x)^(2n) has 2n+1 terms, an odd count, so the single middle term is at position (2n+1+1)/2 = n+1 (checked for n = 1, 2, 3, 4).
General term C(10,r)(-2)^r x^(20-r); 20 - r = 16 gives r = 4, so the coefficient is C(10,4)(-2)^4 = 210*16 = 3360 (sympy expansion agrees).
(x+1/x)^10 gives x^(10-2r); the 1 contributes r = 5 and the x^2 contributes r = 6, while -2x needs r = 5.5 and drops out, so the constant is C(10,5)+C(10,6) = 462 = C(11,5).
Even powers of x cancel in the difference, leaving only x^1, x^3, x^5, x^7 = 4 terms (sympy expansion returns exactly those four monomials).
The full odd-index sum C(14,1)+...+C(14,13) = 2^13 = 8192; the listed sum stops at C(14,11), so subtract the missing C(14,13) = 14, giving 8178 = 2^13 - 14 (direct summation confirms 8178).
The full even-index sum C(11,0)+...+C(11,10) = 2^10 = 1024; the listed sum omits C(11,0) = 1 and C(11,10) = 11, so it equals 1024 - 12 = 1012 = 2^10 - 12 (direct summation confirms 1012).
(3x+2)^4 has 5 terms, so the middle is the 3rd: C(4,2)(3x)^2(2)^2 = 6*9*4 = 216 x^2, and 216 is the 3rd coefficient whether the expansion is read ascending or descending.
T8 = T(7+1) = C(10,7) x^7, so the coefficient is C(10,7) = 120; option C is C(10,8) = 45, the off-by-one distractor, and is not equal to it.
